comparisons.peer_summary: As of December 28, 2024 and December 30, 2023, one customer accounted for approximately 24% and another for 16% of total consolidated accounts receivable, though the Company does not believe these balances represent significant credit risk due to past collection experience.
comparisons.comparison: Both AMD and NVIDIA disclose specific customer concentrations in their accounts receivable balances for fiscal year 2024. NVIDIA identifies two customers holding 24% and 11% of receivables as of January 28, 2024. AMD similarly discloses that one customer accounted for approximately 24% and another for 16% of total consolidated accounts receivable as of December 28, 2024. Both companies explicitly assess credit risk, with AMD stating it does not believe these balances represent significant credit risk based on past collection experience.

sentences.text: Two customers accounted for 24% and 11% of our accounts receivable balance as of January 28, 2024.
One customer accounted for approximately 24% and another customer accounted for 16% of the total consolidated accounts receivable balance as of December 28, 2024 and December 30, 2023, respectively.

comparisons.peer_topic: Significant Customer Concentration in Revenue and Receivables
comparisons.peer_summary: One customer accounted for 18% and 21% of net accounts receivable as of November 3, 2024 and October 29, 2023, respectively, and represented 28%, 21%, and 20% of net revenue in fiscal years 2024, 2023, and 2022. This customer's revenue was included in the semiconductor solutions segment.
comparisons.comparison: Broadcom and NVIDIA both report significant customer concentration in net accounts receivable for fiscal year 2024. NVIDIA discloses that two customers accounted for 24% and 11% of accounts receivable as of January 28, 2024. Broadcom reports that one customer accounted for 18% and 21% of net accounts receivable as of November 3, 2024, and October 29, 2023, respectively. While both highlight single-digit to low-double-digit concentration levels, Broadcom provides specific revenue attribution context (28% of fiscal 2024 net revenue) for its largest customer.

sentences.text: Two customers accounted for 24% and 11% of our accounts receivable balance as of January 28, 2024.
One customer accounted for 18% and 21% of our net accounts receivable balance as of November 3, 2024 and October 29, 2023, respectively.

comparisons.peer_summary: A substantial majority of trade receivables come from OEMs and ODMs, with the three largest customers representing 47% of net accounts receivable as of December 28, 2024, which management believes does not represent significant credit risk.
comparisons.comparison: Intel and NVIDIA both disclose the concentration of trade receivables among their largest customers. Intel identifies its three largest customers as representing 47% of net accounts receivable as of December 28, 2024, whereas NVIDIA identifies two customers accounting for 24% and 11% (totaling 35%) as of January 28, 2024. Both issuers manage credit risk associated with these concentrations; Intel notes these balances do not represent significant credit risk based on cash flow forecasts and past collection experience, aligning with NVIDIA's implicit focus on receivable composition.

sentences.text: Two customers accounted for 24% and 11% of our accounts receivable balance as of January 28, 2024.

We believe the net accounts receivable balances from our three largest customers (47% as of December 28, 2024) do not represent a significant credit risk, based on cash flow forecasts, balance sheet analysis, and past collection experience.

comparisons.peer_summary: The company performs ongoing global credit evaluations of customers and generally does not require collateral, having historically experienced no material losses on receivables, though concentration risks exist for certain customers.
comparisons.comparison: Micron and NVIDIA both address credit risk management regarding accounts receivable. NVIDIA discloses specific concentrations of accounts receivable with two customers (24% and 11%) as of January 2024. Micron discloses that while no single customer accounted for 10% or more of revenue, it faces concentration of credit risk with respect to receivables of certain customers. Micron further states it performs ongoing global credit evaluations and generally does not require collateral, having historically experienced no material losses on receivables, providing a broader risk management context compared to NVIDIA's specific percentage disclosure.
